messages.author: db320aef0eceecf2
messages.subject: minor ticks in log-plot
parts:
Hi,
I am sure someone can help me.
I would like to add minor tick marks along the y-axis in a logarithmic
plot. In the example below, I would like to have minor tick marks
(about half the size of the major tick marks) at 2*10^3, 3*10^3,
4*10^3 etc.
I would not like to add minor grid lines but only little tick marks. I
tried with scale_y_continuous but did not have any success.

Thanks a lot for your help!
Thomas

a <- seq(from=10,to=1000,by=10)^2
b <-log10(a)

dat <-data.frame(b,a)
p<-ggplot(dat,aes(x=b,y=a))
p+geom_point()+scale_y_log10()

--

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: minor ticks in log-plot
parts:
Hi,

It seems pretty hard with Grid too. Would it be possible for ggplot2
to use native coordinates based on the data for the axes viewports?
That would make them much easier to edit; currently I see no way of
knowing where to place extra tick marks,

library(ggplot2)
p <- qplot(1:10, 1:10, geom="blank")

p

g <- ggplotGrob(p)

# grid.ls(getGrob(g,"axis_h::axis.ticks.segments", grep = T))

grid.edit(gPath("axis_h", "axis.ticks.segments"), grep=TRUE,
gp=gpar(col="red",cex=2),x0 = unit(0.25,"native"),
x1 = unit(0.25,"native"))


I add my vote for optional minor ticks, by-the-way.

Best,

baptiste

messages.subject: Re: minor ticks in log-plot

> It seems pretty hard with Grid too. Would it be possible for ggplot2
> to use native coordinates based on the data for the axes viewports?

The problem is that only works for cartesian coordinates systems. One
day a ggplot2 object might return enough information to make it, easy
but that's probably unfortunately along way in the future.
